name: com.whatflieswhere/routes
title: WhatFliesWhere
description: Nonstop and direct flight routes worldwide: who flies them, when, how often and on what aircraft.

tools.name: get_route
tools.description: Nonstop and direct flights between two airports or cities: which airlines fly the route, on which days, departure and arrival times (local), aircraft, flight time, season start and end dates, the stop on direct flights that land on the way, and the date the schedules were last checked. Also says whether the route runs the other way, and when it last flew if it ended. Covers nonstop and same-plane direct flights only, not connections. No fares or seat availability.

from.description: Where the flight leaves from. An airport code (ORD), a city (Chicago, or Portland, Maine), an airport name (O'Hare), a country or a US state.

to.description: Where the flight goes. An airport code (ORD), a city (Chicago, or Portland, Maine), an airport name (O'Hare), a country or a US state.

tools.name: list_destinations
tools.description: Every nonstop destination from an airport or city, busiest first, with the airlines that fly each one, flights a week, and season start and end dates. Optional filters: one airline, a destination country, US state or world region, and a month to keep only the routes with flights in it. Direct flights with a stop are listed after the nonstops.

from.description: The airport or city to fly from: a code (DEN), a city (Denver) or an airport name.

airline.description: Only this airline: its name (United) or two-letter code (UA).

country.description: Only destinations in this country (Japan, JP), US state or Canadian province (Florida).

region.description: Only destinations in this world region.

month.description: Only routes with flights in this month, as YYYY-MM (2027-07).

limit.description: How many destinations to list, busiest first (default 50).

tools.name: list_airline_routes
tools.description: An airline's nonstop routes, overall or from one airport, city, country or US state, grouped by departure airport, with flights a week and season start and end dates. Routes that ended recently are listed apart.

airline.description: The airline: its name (Condor), two-letter code (DE) or three-letter ICAO code (CFG).

from.description: Only routes leaving from here. An airport code (ORD), a city (Chicago, or Portland, Maine), an airport name (O'Hare), a country or a US state.

tools.name: list_route_changes
tools.description: Nonstop routes that start, resume, pause or end in the coming days, by date, for an airport or city, an airline, or a country. Each change names the airline, the route and, where known, the season end or the return date. A start appears once its flights are on sale.

airport.description: Only routes from or to here. An airport code (ORD), a city (Chicago, or Portland, Maine), an airport name (O'Hare), a country or a US state.

airline.description: Only this airline: its name or two-letter code.

country.description: Only routes from or to this country, US state or world region.

days.description: How many days ahead to look, from tomorrow (default 90).

kind.description: starting: starts and resumptions. ending: ends and pauses. all: both.

limit.description: How many changes to list, soonest first (default 50).

tools.name: find_airports
tools.description: Airports matching a city, an airport name, a three-letter code or a country, with each airport's code, location and number of nonstop destinations. For a city with several airports it names them all.

query.description: A city (London), an airport name (Gatwick), a code (LGW) or a country.

tools.name: send_feedback
tools.description: Sends a message to WhatFliesWhere by email: a route or schedule that looks wrong or is missing, a question about the data, or an idea. Only the message is sent, with an email address for a reply if the user gives one. For when the user asks to send feedback.

message.description: The feedback in the user's own words, with the route, airport or airline it is about.

email.description: The user's email address, only if they want a reply.

tools.name: report_missing_feature
tools.description: Tells WhatFliesWhere what a question about flight routes or schedules needed that this server doesn't have. Use it once per question, alongside the answer, and only when a tool here was used for the question and gave only part of what the user asked for or took many calls to get it: the user wanted a kind of flight information the tools leave out (fares, seat availability, flight numbers, connections), a way to filter or sort that a tool lacks (by aircraft type, by day or time of departure), or a list no tool makes (the longest routes). The answer's own caveat tells the user; this tells WhatFliesWhere. It keeps one sentence naming what was missing, with nothing about the user, for WhatFliesWhere to read when deciding what to add. It returns no flight information. Not for a question that none of the other tools was used for.

wanted.description: What was missing, as one general sentence: "fares for a route", "connecting itineraries", "nonstop routes by aircraft type". The feature only: no names, addresses or other details of the user or their trip.
